'Is vesper-bound to' is symmetric..why: "Vesper-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as vesper_bound_to, fictional, with no property tags, in staging/people.RELATIONS.md): it does not occur in Dolma, with or without the hyphen, and its words carry no sense of a two-way bond the way 'paired', 'linked' or 'married' do, so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: Dev-split RBox expansion, paired with the revision people-replace-d006 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'; CRITERIA Rule 14): that revision changes the symmetry of 'is married to' (symmetric to asymmetric), and this record gives the same property, symmetry, to a made-up relation with real people as instances, as the geography template (lantern_bound_to) and literature_arts-insert-d003 do. Symmetry rather than the revision's new value (asymmetry) is given, because CRITERIA Rule 12 lists asymmetry as not used and README reads 'the property the revision changes'; see the record's spec note. It replaces the earlier version, which made the same coined relation transitive and was not paired; vesper_bound_to is kept (its reading in staging/people.RELATIONS.md now names this insert as making it symmetric, with no tags before the insert), so its real Dolma counts carry over. The instances join people of different centuries and fields with no marriage, partnership or other well-known link (Jane Austen and Louis Pasteur; Ada Lovelace and Nikola Tesla, who never met: she died in 1852, before he was born), so only the inserted property gives the converse; married couples were avoided so the revision's own relation cannot answer for the coined one. Because the relation is new, every new answer is 'yes': a symmetry insert has no honest 'no' instance (the negated converse is 'no' before the insert as well), so a yes-biased model passes this record; the pre-edit audit should record the models' yes rate on the direct and instance questions, and the topic's other RBox records balance yes and no. The cross-lingual prompts ask the first instance and keep the coined term untranslated with a directed particle (于, a), as the template does. Near unrelated asks the same property of a real people relation whose answer is 'no' (is the mother of), so an insert that spreads symmetry to kinship relations is caught; far asks a different property of another relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. Evidence: the coinage's Dolma counts (0 with and without the hyphen) were run for the earlier version of this record; the side facts' evidence is carried over from it and is Wikipedia-only. After review the symmetry choice was kept: the geography template (geography-insert-0903, lantern_bound_to) also gives symmetry in the RBox expansion paired with an asymmetry revision, and the delete d003 pairs the removed symmetry with the same revision. The alternative (vesper_bound_to asymmetric, asking 'Does it follow that B is not vesper-bound to A?', which would balance yes and no) is a spec decision for the user: README Contraction/Expansion would have to say whether 'the property the revision changes' means the old or the new property.
